notes.title: NEW INTEL - Introducing the TENNULI
notes.content:
Welcome to EREBUS, a devastated land hiding many mysteries. To understand more about the world of UNYIELDER, it’s time to deep dive into the factions that shaped it. Some are already gone, but what remains can be felt in the current battles. Others are still here, in a different shape. 

Let’s start with the TENNULI:

The TENNULI represent a few groups of Tribes that create fuel by grinding rust from the remnants of old skyscrapers into fine powder. This creates an aerosolised dust fuel that is used to power generators, machinery, and Vulcans.

Sent by the WORLD GOVERNMENT for the pneuma war, the Tennuli prioritize war and fighting. When the blackout occurs, they are left stranded in Erebus with all support cut off. Hence, they can only survive the way they know how - fighting their way through everything else. 

Don’t miss out on our following intel about EREBUS’ factions!

notes.title: NEW INTEL - Sounds of EREBUS - Episode I
notes.content:
Welcome to another INTEL: this time, we’ll explore the sounds of EREBUS. And what makes UNYIELDER so unique: ambient sounds, but also what contributes to the identity of the weapons, the cries of the tormented bosses, and the WOOSH of the desperate dash before the ultimate fall in front of a stronger enemy.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/d59aeddf4b86527fbcb863310ab7174265ef2725.png[/img]

For this first episode, meet Viraj Ramsharan, the sound engineer artist behind the Bismarck’s pleasing sound of destruction.

“The lore of this weapon made it such an interesting weapon to design for. It's one that has been plucked from history, stripped straight off a battleship and slung onto the players shoulder for the ultimate mixture of decimation and power…

When creating the sound for the Bismarck, I wanted the player to really feel the weight and grandeur this weapon offers. One of my favourite things to do with weapons (especially bigger weapons) is to create a rhythm - here there's the initial firing mechanism of the shell propelling for which I used a metal impact, then a brief punchy burst sound followed by the thunderous tail - I used some explosion layers in both of them.

The team at TrueWorld have done a truly amazing job at designing incredible assets and giving us such detailed references to work alongside that really sparked our creativity! One of my favourite things to do with weapons (especially bigger weapons) is to create a rhythm – here, there's the initial firing mechanism hit of the shell propelling for which I used a metal impact, then a brief punchy burst sound followed by the thunderous tail - I used some explosion layers in both of them.”

What’s your favorite weapon sound effect? Let us know in the comments! 

Stay tuned for the next installation of our series!

notes.title: NEW INTEL! UNYIELDER - PERKS GUIDE Part I
notes.content:
In the ruined world of EREBUS, survival is about your skills and weapons. Once you beat a major boss, they might drop random perks in their lootbox and they can be game-changing, with the right combination.
 
To unlock superior Tiers drop chance, you'll have to explore the Mastery Tree and spend your available points.
 
To create the meta that will suit you, in addition to the weapon attachments that are randomized:  you'll have to be patient and you'll have to make the right decisions before EREBUS and its bosses catch you up.
 
Here's a list of the current available perks:


[h1]Tier 1[/h1]

[b]ARSONIST[/b] – Increases burn damage
[b]BLESSING [/b]– Chance for more ammo on pickup
[b]BREEZE[/b] – Increases movespeed
[b]DEEP POCKETS[/b] – Increases the total amount of ammo the player can hold
[b]IMPATIENCE[/b] – Decreases ability cooldown
[b]LATTICE BATTERY[/b] – Increases max shields
[b]PERSONAL COURTESY[/b] – Decreases melee cooldown
[b]PYRO [/b]– Increases burn duration
[b]RATTLER[/b] – Increases fire rate, increases recoil
[b]SIPHON[/b] – Increases heavy ammo drop chance
[b]SPEEDLOADERS [/b]– Decreases reload time, decreases magazine size
[b]STENDO [/b]– Increases magazine size, increases reload time
[b]VITALITY [/b]– Increases max health

[h1]Tier 2[/h1]

[b]AGNI[/b] – Melee attacks have a chance to set enemies on fire
[b]CONTINGENCY [/b]– On Death: Revive with health. This perk and all its stacks are consumed when activated. Any amount above full health will be granted as overheal. Each extra perk level will grant additional health on revive
[b]DEMOLITIONER [/b]– Increases explosive damage
[b]HEATSINKS[/b] – Increases dash cooldown rate
[b]LATTICE AURA [/b]– Evasive action will create an aura with range. Causes shield to continuously recharge. The aura lasts for a few seconds. While within the aura, damage will not stop the shield from recharging
[b]LATTICE OVERCLOCK[/b] – Increases shield regen rate
[b]MANIA [/b]– While at low HP, increases crit chance. Shields do not count towards HP threshold
[b]MISSING BULLET [/b]– Increases chance to not consume ammo when firing
[b]RESILIENCE[/b] – When at low HP, decreases damage taken. Deactivates if player's health increases above breakpoint again. Shields do not count as HP
[b]ROOK[/b] – If damage is negated by the invincibility frames of an evasive action, instantly refill a section of dash bar
[b]SLICK[/b] – If not hit after a while of entering an arena, increases crit damage for the rest of the fight
SPEEDLOADER AURA – Evasive action will create an aura with range. Decreases the player's reload time. The aura lasts for a few seconds and can only be placed again after the aura expires
[b]SPIKEDRIVER [/b]– While sliding, increases melee lunge range
[b]SPLINTERSHOT[/b] – Increases multishot, decreases firerate
[b]THRIFTY[/b] – Increases ammo efficiency

[h1]Tier 3[/h1]

[b]ABADDON AURA[/b] – On Counterhit, deploy an aura with range at player location. While in the aura, increases crit chance. Lasts for a few seconds, only a single instance is allowed — new instances override
[b]CLOSE TO GROUND [/b]– Shooting after sliding increases multishot
[b]DEFENSIVE OFFENCE[/b] – If damage is negated by the invincibility frames of an evasive action, next shot increases multishot
[b]ENERGY RELEASE[/b] – Taking damage causes the player to deal damage to enemies in an area around themselves
Damage: Fixed amount
Area size: Fixed range
[b]ENGORGE [/b]– Increases health gained per health pickup
[b]FUTURE PLANNING[/b] – A portion of the damage that the player does is stored and gets converted into shields when the player uses their evasive action
[b]GUNBOATS[/b] – Decreases self-damage, decreases damage from explosions
[b]LIBIDO [/b]– Increases crit chance, decreases HP (Perk CAN kill player)
[b]LOOTERPULSE [/b]– Every so often, a radial pulse is released from the player. This pulse automatically collects all ammo pickups it touches
When Stacking: Decreases cooldown, increases pulse radius
[b]PHASESTRIKER [/b]– Increases crit chance during phase break
When damaging enemies (per instance): Chance for a grenade to spawn from the point of impact. This grenade deals extra damage based on the instance of damage which spawned it
[b]RETRIBUTION[/b] – Taking damage from an enemy increases crit chance for a few seconds (Stacks)
[b]THAUM [/b]– Increases KAMI weapon recharge rate
[b]THE FIREBRAND [/b]– Increases health for every burn tick on an enemy (Stacks)
[b]HOUNDSTOOTH[/b] – When damaging enemies (per instance): Chance for a grenade to spawn from the point of impact. This grenade deals extra damage based on the instance of damage which spawned it

But don't think that you will master the PERKS of UNYIELDER that easily: more of them are waiting for you in the darkness of EREBUS, so stay tuned for the definitive guide. Let us know in the comments the one you enjoyed the most!

notes.title: [NEW INTEL] EREBUS' Score - Songs from Chaos - Part III - HAZEL HO
notes.content:
The third composer is Hazel Ho, a musician from Singapore, who graduated Summa Cum Laude in Contemporary Writing and Production from the prestigious Berklee College of Music in 2023. The heart of her art lies in live instruments, with rather avant-garde jazz inspirations. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/b24f39a514d01c5a503e05c093ab8af0d298d43d.png[/img]

For UNYIELDER and TrueWorld Studios, she stepped away from her usual genre to draw inspirations from rock, metal, and distorted, glitchy production techniques, perhaps marking a new era for Hazel Ho. She handled the themes for SKINNER and PRETENDER. She drew from the roots of Andalusian music to bring her melody: [i]“I was diving into the flamenco genre for SKINNER's theme, so the first few iterations were very flamenco-driven. Imagine: Cajon, castanets, flamenco Guitar, orchestral elements, with Andalusian cadences. No rock or metal elements yet. The reactions were hilarious - the meeting room burst into laughter over this direction for SKINNER (in a good way!), and people were even starting to think about adding cactuses in the arena. I later on added those rock/metal elements to up the aggressiveness! PRETENDER's track has a touch of a bassline in 5/8 in one section that I love! Can't help myself with odd meters sometimes! Also, this entire track is a big step into the production realm for me personally!”[/i]

And that’s all from our maestros of chaos! Stay tuned for our next instalment as we speak to the sound designers of Pitstop - the ones who created the satisfying rat-at-tats of the guns!

notes.title: [NEW INTEL] EREBUS' Score - Songs from Chaos - Part II - HOHENHEIM
notes.content:
Enter Hohenheim, the mysterious, the demon, a veteran of the industry. His hypnotic sounds, heart-beat-like percussions, his entire universe gives a sense of urgency, relentless, a powerful macabre dance that eventually becomes one with EREBUS. In the language of demons, there is no word for “restraint”. 
[b]That’s probably why TrueWorld gave the MARAETH to Hohenheim, a faction best known for its zealousness and mania[/b]. If you listen closely, you can hear the MARAETH’s sea of voices chanting, like an infernal siren song. For most, that’s terrifying. For a demon, a lullaby. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/58358a3d2a80da9460d348c69a2cfbc74df00ba9.jpg[/img]

And when asked about his inspirations, Hohenheim responds: [i]“Oh, you want me to write a theme for a tortured god caged in a child’s body? How? Crank that orchestra until your skull buzzes. That's how. And that’s why yours truly recommends one of the late bosses’ tracks as well as the track for when you first meet the MARAETH. For the late boss, I started composing it sweet - like really sweet. Smooth and dramatic strings, a whole romantic era composition that stands well on its own. But then - oh, yes, that’s when I spiked the drink. Ripped it apart. Let mechanical shrieks tear into that orchestra, warp that melody with the “Kzzzzzrrch!” of a cyborg's temper tantrum. Full audio meltdown, baby. Why? [b]Surely us humans love nothing more than to overload the brain.[/b] Find that sweet spot between licking a battery and chugging a bottle of spiked cough syrup. Devour that mania, let it pour down your throat, set your synapses ablaze. Makes you feel what it's like to be the late boss, methinks. And suddenly, boom, you just made the soundtrack. 

[b]As for MARAETH… want to really feel how far the organic can twist until it’s shredded into its mechanical parts? Only to brute force it back into shape again until you’re left with something so mangled it stops making sense[/b] – but still pulses like it’s alive? Hell, do I have something for you then. Look no further than their main theme. It’s basically all cello and no synth, baby. Here’s to your all too familiar, friendly, classy instrument played with claws, not fingers. The melodies and motifs are still kind of there, though, but eroded and in scraps, as if they were once whole but replayed so often that little of the original tape remains intact. It’s that sweet madness creeping in, the sense that something big and wrong is about to happen. You know you shouldn’t welcome it. Hope you’re ready for the ride!”[/i]

If you made it here alive and not entirely mesmerized by Hohenheim… Don’t miss our next portrait!

notes.title: [NEW INTEL] EREBUS' Score - Songs from Chaos - Part I - KARU
notes.content:
If chaos is part of EREBUS's DNA, traversing its devastated corridors and facing its untamed inhabitants wouldn't be complete without the unique themes and music written for UNYIELDER.
Three composers lent their talents to give a unique character to the bosses, characters, and overall atmosphere of UNYIELDER, bringing EREBUS and its dangers to life. Each composer brings their expertise, peculiarities, and vision to the ravaged universe of UNYIELDER. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/bb82b9a0fa89de75648f86f902e655e67edb34dd.jpg[/img]

Let’s meet Karu - whose real name is Carl Abelgas, a 23-year-old composer from the Philippines, celebrates his first milestone in the video game world. [i]"I wanted each of the bosses or factions to have their own distinct themes through differing motifs and instrumentations. The TENNULI, for example, being a rather militaristic and war-hungry faction, I took a more aggressive approach but with substantial scale, such as the use of heavy brass, and snare drums layered with electric guitars. Furthermore, I had some chants added to emulate battle cries. With the IMPERIUM, I aimed to make it sound more regal, but with a touch of unpredictability. The instrumentation leaned more towards a traditional symphonic orchestra, but as the battle progresses, the scale and key keep changing."[/i]

The music in UNYIELDER not only dresses the environment and battles but also accompanies the player in their quest for power, changing as they delve deeper into their torment. [i]“I didn’t want this to be purely a theme for the boss and characters, but I wanted to consider the player as they fought them. As the battle progresses, the composition changes slightly to make the player feel more of a badass, adding impact and that “oomf” to the gameplay. I won’t spoil too much on this front, but you’ll be able to feel it yourself when the game comes out! I'd reckon RAIN's Theme and one of the later bosses is a lot of fun too right now!”[/i]


That’s it for now. Don’t miss our next musical encounter, a very special one, an encounter that only EREBUS can hold.

notes.title: UNYIELDER Prologue Demo Patch Notes: CS38786
notes.content:
Thank you all for enjoying the UNYIELDER Prologue Demo thus far! Per your feedback, we've also made some changes. Do remember to update your demo files if you haven't, and see you again in EREBUS!

For the nitty and the gritty, please read below - 

[b]Changes[/b]
[u]General[/u]
[list]
[*] Actual portraits added to replace the older placeholder portraits
[*] Generally reduced package size of the builds
[*] Difficulty scaling rebalanced. Scaling should now be relatively minor for the first few levels, and will start scaling up close to when the Outpost begins appearing in the Stage Select
[/list]
[u]UI[/u]
[list]
[*] Enlarged mastery tree
[*] All UI backgrounds have been changed
[*] You should now be able to customize the keybind for Crouch/Slide
[*] You should now be able to correctly swap weapons using the scroll wheel
[*] You should now be able to customize the keybind for the different gun slots
[*] Reduced the size of the skip and auto text displays on the Dialogue screen
[*] Visual changes to the indicator for Grapple Fist
[/list]

[b]Fixed Bugs[/b]
[u]General[/u]
[list]
[*] If continuing a run from a mid-run save, the player's health will no longer be restored to full this way
[*] Settings related issues fixed
[*] Effects Quality
[*] Anti-aliasing options
[*] Players can no longer set mouse sensitivity values to 0
[*] Settings menu navigation issues resolved
[*] Fixed an issue that has a chance of bringing the player back to the Base when Cavity is selected after the tutorial has concluded
[/list]
[u]Bosses[/u]
[list]
[*] Bosses should no longer leave their various effects behind when the player loses to the boss, or when the player yields, returns to the player base, then starts a new run
[*] Especially Monolith's Trophy Barrier
[*] Dredger's flaming trails should now correctly deal tick damage to the player as long as the player is within those trails
[*] Rain should no longer drop the items that she would otherwise only drop if she is defeated in full (which should not happen in the demo)
[*] Fixed some inconsistencies with Hopper's hops jumps
[*] Made some changes to Dredger and Hopper to make it less likely for them to go into terrain during some attacks
[/list]
[u]Guns[/u]
[list]
[*] Artifact should now be able to be picked up normally
[/list]
[u]Perks[/u]
[list]
[*] Slick no longer retains its buff effects after the boss has died, and will no longer apply its timed buff if the player yields immediately after a boss spawns. There should no longer be any way for the player to stack this perk's effects
[*] Mania now updates its buff effects when the perk is levelled up, if the player manages to not heal enough health to deactivate the buff while this is happening. The perk's icon should also now correctly show up and disappear as the associated buff is acquired and removed from the player
[*] Pyro's Tier 3 buff now correctly applies on burn tick rather than on burn application. This buff should also fall off now as soon as the boss is defeated or when the run ends
[*] Lattice Aura should correctly start the shield regeneration process as soon as any shield value is lost (and should no longer stop you from regenerating shield)
[*] Bombardiers no longer briefly generates a little buff indicator when that little bomb drops behind the player on Dash
[*] Contingency's overheal no longer persists after a run ends
[/list]
[u]Weapon Mods[/u]
[list]
[*] Quadloader now no longer only consumes 1 shot's worth of ammunition when loading more than 1 shot into the chamber
[*] Skinner's Tuning should now deduct ammunition correctly and consistently
[*] Sensitive Magazine now does not double magazine size without perk modifiers, and should now take into consideration perk values
[/list]
[u]UI[/u]
[list]
[*] Disabled scroll wheel for mastery
[*] Fixed Sell button not functioning when a player attempts to put a Data Drive into the Sell Menu
[*] The Mastery Points UI popup when leveling up should now show the correct number of Mastery Points gained.
[*] The player's inventory should now load correctly when accessing the sell menu
[*] The General Stats Results Screen should now show the correct values
[/list]
[u]Misc[/u]
[list]
[*] Bunch of other under the hood changes that should improve overall performance
[/list]

[u]Known issues[/u]
[list]
[*] The newly added voice and sound effects volume controls are not currently saving correctly.
[/list]

Enjoy the freshly updated EREBUS and remember... 
[b][i]NEVER YIELD.[/i][/b]

notes.title: UNYIELDER Prologue Demo - The New Arsenal
notes.content:
EREBUS just got bigger. Wilder. And with brand new threats, you’ll get a chance to try new weapons. CALDERA, DOWNPOUR, and BASTET are available for you to include in your build.

[h1]CALDERA, the Rocket Launcher[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/567995be9bcaaf5ff76bf865e312e13fdb38b510.jpg[/img]

CALDERA is a brutal rocket launcher. It uses heavy ammo and primary fire is a literal straightforward shot: the rocket will fly in a straight line and explode in contact. Secondary fire is bringing a tactical side and will allow you to reposition easily: it will lock the target determined by your crosshair, and has semi-tracking capabilities that will allow you to track down the target as long as the movements aren’t too sudden. Finish a boss in style with a powerful shot of CALDERA!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/876707cb2c3817d79e7dd8b8cedbe71ccc1b6c17.gif[/img]

[h1]DOWNPOUR, the Automatic Rifle
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/2bc6c4b86d34d5a6fc90dec02cf47929dbef4155.png[/img]

DOWNPOUR is an automatic rifle equipped with a drum magazine on the side. Hold down primary to increase its fire rate, and use secondary to toggle the aiming sight. The reload time will take a bit longer, but that’s the price for a bigger capacity. And beware of the vertical recoil. This will make a deadly pair with powerful single shot weapons such as BISMARCK or CALDERA. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/0654ccb5a564601d1954f86d9c0d06a73cbf29c8.gif[/img]

[h1]BASTET, the Revolver
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/d0065094d0f8d328ca23de16cebfa25dba1d1518.png[/img]

BASTET is a Revolver and will behave like so: quick fire with a lot of recoil and 6 shots by default, so make them count! Beware of the perks you will use or the mods that you’ll be dealt with, that can significantly reduce the overall ammo capacity, BASTET is still a great ally to have in your meta during the Prologue Demo. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/2da7aa479aee5694329a4728ab727e43ef670f6d.gif[/img]

So far, which one is your favorite? Did you wield all of them?

Let us know your current build! And don’t forget… Never yield!

notes.title: UNYIELDER Prologue is here - brace for impact!
notes.content:
Greetings, PRETENDERS,

We are proud to announce the release of UNYIELDER’s Prologue Demo, ahead of the Steam Next Fest. It is now time to reveal a glimpse of what this world has to offer: while the Combat Demo was focused on the shooting mechanics, this one will give you a wider understanding of the final game. 

New Weapons to reinforce your arsenal: DOWNPOUR, BASTET, and CALDERA. ARTIFACT, the shotgun, has been reworked for a more substantial impact. New Weapons and New Perks also mean… New Deadly Enemies. 

ROOK is the newest addition to the roster of bosses. And they might not be the only danger lurking in the corridors of EREBUS. If you were getting too familiar with the maps, rejoice: New Playgrounds will be introduced in this demo for you to explore and master: the outpost RIDGELINE and the DEPOT. BASILICA and HOUSE OF CARDS, your base, are two more peaceful zones to explore.

We also heard your feedback: the UI has been entirely reworked, perks are easier to read and thus include in your build, and combat mechanics have been improved. Torment will also raise more regularly, to give you a stronger challenge.

Please note that your progression from this Demo to the final game will be saved. 

So, TO ARMS PRETENDERS! It’s time to conquer a brand new territory and rediscover UNYIELDER. Don’t forget to WISHLIST, rate us on Steam, and send us your feedback! Thank you for your support.

notes.title: THANK YOU! Sunsetting the Combat Demo
notes.content:
Greetings, PRETENDERS,

It’s time for us to bid farewell to the Combat Demo. Your first introduction to EREBUS, ANTARKTA, led you to meet HATCHLING, HOPPER, or even GARRISON in the guts of a devastated wasteland. You had to learn the hard way to master ARTIFACT, ANTIOCH, INTERLOPER, OCELOT, SWANSONG, and the mighty BISMARCK. And now you think you’ve made your way in UNYIELDER?

This is not the end of the road.

This is just the beginning.

New Intel will drop in a few days. New places to fight. New bosses to dominate. New perks and new weapons to overcome the toughest challenges. New answers to your questions. 

The path to the Truth is long. Thank you for coming alongside.

Will you survive?

Stay tuned. Stay sharp. Get ready for the next challenge.

notes.title: TOOLS OF DESTRUCTION - ANTIOCH
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/aa53eb9023d5dcb7b4f22ca96f978f13bb832664.jpg[/img]

Antioch is a powerful grenade-launcher. It uses special ammo to launch unique grenades: they can stick to the surfaces and have a delayed explosion, or to explode in contact. While its primary shot fires three rounds that bounce and detonate with time, the secondary shot fires a single sticky shot that explodes on release - or whenever Antioch is empty. You may want to use the primary shot when escaping and leave a deadly path behind you. Just make sure to stay away from the area of effect: as with the Bismarck, Antioch can be deadly to you too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/173e4e747094a0162c8cbd058395490bde19cbce.gif[/img]

Antioch is not your regular grenade launcher. Its power will get even stronger if you master the environment and stick the right grenade at the right place and the right time. Since its reloading time is quick, while dealing a lot of damage, Antioch is a very precious ally. Keep an eye on your ammo, though, it can be very quick to be depleted. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/12361a8739ad792917dba443709f3f44b82ebfcc.gif[/img]

Depending on your style, we suggest using Antioch with Interloper and Swansong for a good mix between DPS and movement if you have a good aim, or Ocelot and Artifact if you’re opting for a more aggressive build.

Check out Antioch’s full infography here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/d657a9fb01f24bea386aac8ff43f35f43a27548d.png[/img]

notes.title: TOOLS OF DESTRUCTION - INTERLOPER - SEMI-AUTOMATIC PISTOL
notes.content:
With its high fire rate, Interloper is a great weapon to start with. Using light ammo, this semi-automatic pistol will balance an aggressive but slower build with Artifact and Bismarck for instance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/69e432f4e185d05f271aafe8870591f409502f93.jpg[/img]

You may be tempted to empty your magazine on the enemy, but keep your sight on the target: Interloper’s recoil can surprise you. You might want to train before jumping into your next fight equipped with this bad boy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/bdf16b9543b1e8d40d5a9ee61dc9bac96581e549.gif[/img]

You can quickly fire it to your target to reposition or counter the boss, or wait for the right moment to use the secondary fire: the charged shot. With its damages based on the amount of bullets you have left in your magazine, it goes well with a perk increasing the mag capacity. Beware of the downside: it consumes the entire mag and has a short delay before shooting. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/05c8be1b211e945a2545b1c2ea2e06f0d4270b43.gif[/img]

So lock and load, stay steady, and go show them who’s the boss.

Play UNYIELDER's Combat Demo now before it's too late!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/789940/UNYIELDER/

notes.title: TOOLS OF DESTRUCTION - BISMARCK
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/073911c876801f3c9d08b519ef951f9ba4448f46.jpg[/img]

The Bismarck is pure destruction in your hands. This single-shot cannon delivers devastating power with special ammo, dealing a significant amount of damage in its area of effect. Precision isn’t its goal—chaos is.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/bc1d451d4af8982784dd2771b7fb1388784a3b74.gif[/img]

However, its power comes with a trade-off: a long reload time. Timing is key, so pair it with a quick-firing weapon like the Interloper or Ocelot to cover your reload and maintain control at all ranges. Use it during critical moments, when the boss is stunned and – for a short time – vulnerable, to take the advantage.

Keep your distance—the Bismarck’s blast is indiscriminate, and a mistimed shot could hurt you as much as your target. Master its potential, and you’ll become a battlefield legend.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/e80b5a9061f7d665b45619f735f3ffa5e87ef9b2.gif[/img]

Lock, load, and unleash chaos—are you ready to dominate?

notes.title: Tools of Destruction - Swansong
notes.content:
Greetings, Pretender. Here's the time for another guide! Introducing Swansong, the perfect weapon for dominating from a distance while staying agile and aggressive. Its immense damage output and versatility make it a tool for both precise and bold play.

[img]https://media1.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExOHNxNHRjMnpjNHliZnE5NjFsb2N3ZWVlZ2F6cDV1dm1lMTFqenNnbiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/HHEF5L9h3yVnNiTjom/giphy.gif[/img]

[h1]Immense Damage Without Aiming[/h1]

The main fire deals massive damage, even without aiming, making it perfect for quick, reactive shots in close-to-mid-range combat.

[h1]Scoped Multi-Shot[/h1]

Holding right-click lets you fire multiple rounds, increasing your chances to hit moving or distant targets.

[h1]Repositioning Power[/h1]

After each shot, reposition to stay unpredictable. Swansong rewards mobility and smart angles.

[h1]Long-Range Precision[/h1]

Ideal for staying safe while eliminating threats from a distance.

Always keep an eye on the distance and spot the perfect timing to breach the bosses. With the right balance between repositioning and aggression, Swansong is your best friend to dominate the battlefield. While it can be long to reload, always keep with you a revolver or a handgun to mitigate any surprise attacks from the bosses, and rule Erebus with your own vision.

notes.title: Tools of Destruction - Artifact - Unleash Destruction
notes.content:
Greetings, Pretenders,

You think you’ve got what it takes? Let’s see how well you fare with a weapon that demands skill, precision, and the nerve to get close enough to taste your enemy’s fury: meet Artifact, a powerful shotgun. This isn’t for the faint of heart—it’s a tool of raw power for those who embrace risk.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/9ab063b4b7b3e64ba9488ee5161a179286343edc.gif[/img]

[h1]Fast. Bold. Relentless. But Know Your Limits.
[/h1]
The shotgun is not a forgiving weapon. It thrives in the chaos of close quarters, where hesitation is fatal. Don’t even think about using it at range—leave that to the rocket launcher (we’ll deal with that beast later). Every shot, every shell, every step must have purpose. Use your grapple to close the distance fast, aim for the weak spots, and leave nothing but devastation in your wake.

[h1]Patience is a Killer’s Weapon
[/h1]
This is no spray-and-pray toy. Artifact rewards precision and timing. Miss your shot, and you’ll be staring down a boss that has no mercy for your mistakes. Its slow reload demands discipline—waste a shell, and it might be your last. The blink of an eye is all you’ll get, so don’t miss your opportunity to strike.

[h1]Precision or Devastation—Choose Wisely
[/h1]
Artifact is more than a weapon—it’s a statement. Left-click delivers a single, focused blast for precision damage, while right-click lets you unleash three rounds that bounce, turning chaos into carnage. The main fire channels precision; the secondary fire spreads destruction. Use both wisely—they’ll save you or bury you.

Pair Artifact with intent. For maximum devastation, go heavy—a big gun that complements your shotgun’s burst damage. But be warned: heavy weapons slow you down, and hesitation will get you killed. Want to stay nimble? Pair it with a fast-paced weapon like Interloper, to pepper enemies between brutal shotgun blasts, giving you room to reposition and survive.

Take up your shotgun, Pretender. Prove you’re not just another corpse in Erebus. You’re here to fight, to endure, to rise. Now, deliver devastation and show the void what defiance looks like.

[i]🔥 "Every blast of Artifact is a rebellion, a thunderclap against the chaos that seeks to consume you." 🔥[/i]

notes.title: Tools of Destruction - The Ocelot
notes.content:
[b]Greetings, Pretenders.[/b]

The dark halls of UNYIELDER are no place for mercy, and your revolver is more than a weapon—it’s your fleeting promise of survival. Today, we dive into the ruthless art of Revolver Gunplay, a skill that separates the fallen from the unbroken.

[h1]Two Ways to Shoot, One Shot to Survive[/h1]

In UNYIELDER, gunfights are raw and unforgiving. Ocelot, the revolver, offers two distinct styles of play, each tailored to the chaos of battle:

[h2]Rapid Fire (Default: Left Click)[/h2]

Embrace the fury of desperation. Spam-clicking unleashes a storm of lead, sacrificing precision for raw speed. It’s a lifeline in the heat of close combat, disrupting enemies and forcing a critical gap between you and the relentless bosses. In those frantic moments, this is your chance to breathe, reposition, and prepare for the next blow.

[h2]Precision Aim[/h2]

For those who dare to steady their hand, precision aim brings calculated lethality to the fight. Once you’ve secured distance, this method rewards your focus with increased damage and accuracy, turning the tide of battle in your favor. Every shot counts—and every miss could cost you dearly.

[h3]Reload Fast. Think Faster.[/h3]

Ocelot isn’t just a tool; it’s a promise to yourself that you can claw your way out, no matter how grim the odds. Its rapid reload ensures you’re never defenseless for long, giving you the edge to seize even the smallest opportunity. Every second, every movement, every bullet—it’s all or nothing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43796707/4f1eda94eebae5b728856d3e42b5a6b6722e8cae.gif[/img]

So, Pretender, [b]the question is simple:[/b]

Can you handle the weight of survival? Or will you become just another whisper in the halls of UNYIELDER?

[b]Lock, load, and prove your worth.
[/b]

notes.title: Welcome to Erebus, Antarctica: The Combat Demo Awaits
notes.content:
[b]Greetings, Pretenders.[/b]

The time has come to step into the icy depths of Erebus, Antarctica, a place as unforgiving as the fate of mankind itself. Here, in the shadow of a crumbling world, your journey begins—not with answers, but with battle.

Today, the UNYIELDER Combat Demo launches, offering you the chance to experience the heart of what defines this unforgiving world: [b]the fight for survival.[/b] This demo is your gateway to the raw, unrelenting combat mechanics that form the core of the game. It’s a test of your skill, determination, and ability to rise after every fall.

This demo is more than just an introduction—it’s a preview, focused solely on the combat system that captivated audiences during our recent physical event. The overwhelmingly positive reception inspired us to ensure that everyone could experience these mechanics firsthand. We want you to enjoy the challenge, immerse yourself in the fight, and share your feedback with us before we take the next step.
But be warned—this is only the beginning. In this demo, answers to the questions that haunt you[b]—why you were retrieved from a mysterious facility, why you’re here, and what your purpose is—[/b]remain tantalizingly out of reach. Instead, your focus will be survival, your progression measured by how well you can overcome the bosses that stand in your way.

Stay vigilant, Pretenders. A more complete demo, with expanded features and deeper insights into the mysteries of this world, is on the horizon. For now, prove your worth in the icy crucible of Erebus.

[h1]A World of Combat and Challenge[/h1]

Erebus is a cold, hostile environment built to test even the most resolute. As the Pretender, you will step into this desolate world and face combat mechanics designed to challenge every decision you make. With every enemy you confront, you’ll learn the intricacies of timing, positioning, and strategy that are key to mastering UNYIELDER.

This is not a place to uncover truths just yet. Instead, it’s a proving ground—a crucible where you hone your skills and prepare for the greater challenges to come. You’ll face bosses in epic 1v1 fights, who will punish the unprepared and who will push your limits. Victory is earned, not given.

[previewyoutube=pAl3TAY2A5k;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]What Awaits in the Combat Demo[/h1]

[list]
[*] [b]Immersive Combat Mechanics:[/b] Experience the precision-based fighting system that defines UNYIELDER. Every encounter is a test of your skill, with epic bosses fights that demand mastery, patience, skills. Use up to the 6 weapons available in this limited time Combat Demo, and create your perfect combo to get it out alive.

[*] [b]This is not about the why, it’s about survival: [/b]This is not the time for answers—yet. It's the time to fight. The Combat Demo gives you only a glimpse of the mysterious world of Erebus, offering hints of its secrets but withholding the answers for you to discover in the full game.

[*] [b]Prepare for the Challenge: [/b]You are the Pretender, and every moment in the demo is designed to push you further, demanding adaptability and resolve.
[/list]

[h1]The Journey Begins NOW[/h1]

The UNYIELDER Combat Demo launches today, at 6PM GMT. Are you ready to step into the boots of the Pretender and face the relentless challenges of Erebus? This demo is only a taste of what’s to come—a chance to test your skills against mighty bosses who will not go down easily. 
Prepare to fight, fall, and rise again. This is your moment to prove yourself.

[h1]Will You Rise?[/h1]

Wishlist UNYIELDER on Steam now, and take your first step into the fray on December 17. The journey to your own survival begins with your ability to endure—and conquer. Don't forget to share your feedback on the Discord server!
